LESSON: WRITING 1.4.1 PRE- WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Writing 1.4.1 Pre- writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.4.1 Pre- writing, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to sit properly when writing? How do we place our books when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.4.1 Pre- writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced as they practise holding pencils correctly and write from the left to the

right.

Creativity and imagination: learner’s ability to make decisions is enhanced as they undertake activities that require selection of right and

effective course for the purpose of achieving a desired result through drawing and colouring patterns and shapes.

Values:
Responsibility: is developed as the learner gains self-drive to practise holding pencils or colouring materials correctly.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Learner support programmes: Clubs and societies are enhanced as learners uses drawing and colouring skills in art clubs with peers.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Kiswahili Language Activities: as the pre-writing skills are emphasised as learners practise to sit in appropriate sitting posture in preparation

for writing.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Pictures, videos, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital

devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
